# Example Solution 1

## **Part 0: libraries**

```{r}
library(tidyverse)
library(sf)
library(maps)
library(ggplot2)
```

## **Part 1:** **Defining Research Question**

Chosen Question: Are EV registrations concentrated in states with a higher percentage of renewable energy in their total energy use?

## **Part 2: Data Preparation and Cleaning**
```{r}
renew_use_2021 <- read_csv("data/renew-use-2021.csv", show_col_types = FALSE)
renew_use_2022 <- read_csv("data/renew-use-2022.csv", show_col_types = FALSE)
renew_use_2023 <- read_csv("data/renew-use-2023.csv", show_col_types = FALSE)

av_energy_price <- read_csv("data/av-energy-price-2021-2023.csv", show_col_types = FALSE)

total_energy_use_2021 <- read_csv("data/total-use-2021.csv", show_col_types = FALSE)
total_energy_use_2022 <- read_csv("data/total-use-2022.csv", show_col_types = FALSE)
total_energy_use_2023 <- read_csv("data/total-use-2023.csv", show_col_types = FALSE)


ev_registrations_2023 <- read_csv("data/ev-registrations-by-state-2023.csv", show_col_types = FALSE)

# --- Define a safer cleaning function ---
clean_data <- function(df) {
  df |>
    janitor::clean_names() |>     # Clean names (lowercase, underscores, removes symbols)
    mutate(across(where(is.character), str_trim)) |>  # Trim extra spaces
    { if ("state" %in% names(.)) {                    # Standardize state names if present
        mutate(., state = str_to_title(state))
      } else { . }
    }
}

renew_use_2021 <- clean_data(renew_use_2021)
renew_use_2022 <- clean_data(renew_use_2022)
renew_use_2023 <- clean_data(renew_use_2023)

av_energy_price <- clean_data(av_energy_price)
total_energy_use_2021 <- clean_data(total_energy_use_2021)
total_energy_use_2022 <- clean_data(total_energy_use_2022)
total_energy_use_2023 <- clean_data(total_energy_use_2023)
ev_registrations_2023 <- clean_data(ev_registrations_2023)

```

## **Part 3: Joining / Pivoting Datasets for Analysis**
```{r}
renew_use_all <- bind_rows(
  renew_use_2021 |> mutate(year = 2021) |> rename(renewable_use = renewable_use_2021),
  renew_use_2022 |> mutate(year = 2022) |> rename(renewable_use = renewable_use_2022),
  renew_use_2023 |> mutate(year = 2023) |> rename(renewable_use = renewable_use_2023)
) |>
  # Sum up renewable use by state and year
  group_by(state, year) |>
  summarise(
    renew_use_total = sum(renewable_use, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = 'drop'
  ) |>
  filter(year == 2023) |>
  select(state, renew_use_total)
```

## **Part 4: Mapping Visualization**
```{r}
map_renewable_energy <- ggplot(data = map_data) +
  geom_sf(aes(fill = percent_renewable), color = "white", linewidth = 0.1) +
  scale_fill_viridis_c(
    option = "G", 
    direction = -1, 
    name = "Renewable Energy (%)" 
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Share of Renewable Energy in Total Energy Use by State (2023)",
    subtitle = "Higher percentages indicate cleaner energy for EV charging."
  ) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(
    axis.text = element_blank(), 
    axis.title = element_blank(),
    panel.grid = element_blank()
  )

print(map_renewable_energy)

map_ev_registrations <- ggplot(data = map_data) +
  geom_sf(aes(fill = log_ev_registrations), color = "white", linewidth = 0.1) +
  scale_fill_viridis_c(
    option = "D", 
    name = "EV Registrations (Log-Transformed)"
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "EV Registrations by State (2023)",
    subtitle = "Log-transformed for visual clarity."
  ) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(
    axis.text = element_blank(),
    axis.title = element_blank(),
    panel.grid = element_blank()
  )

print(map_ev_registrations)

```
